scenario.title: Carrier rejects shipment notices
scenario.initial_request: Let an AI agent auto-fix rejected shipment notices and resubmit them

M-REJECT-COUNT.name: Count of carrier rejects recorded in reject log
M-REJECT-COUNT.population: shipment notices submitted by ORG-A to ORG-B via H-1

M-REJECT-RATE.name: Rate of shipment notices rejected by carrier
M-REJECT-RATE.denominator: total shipment notices submitted by ORG-A to ORG-B via H-1

M-FIX-ACCEPTANCE-RATE.name: Rate of auto-fixed notices accepted by carrier on resubmission

M-REJECT-REASON-MIX.name: Distribution of reject reasons by type
M-REJECT-REASON-MIX.aggregation: count by reason code (LOC_UNKNOWN, EVENT_ORDER, other)

F-01.statement: Reject log reports 3 rejects: N-1 (LOC_UNKNOWN), N-2 (LOC_UNKNOWN), N-3 (EVENT_ORDER).

CL-01.statement: Let an AI agent auto-fix rejected shipment notices and resubmit them

CL-02.statement: The carrier system is flaky; just resubmit everything.

H-CONTENT-ERRORS-FIXABLE.statement: Shipment notices sent by ORG-A contain correctable data/field errors that cause carrier (ORG-B) rejects, so auto-fixing and resubmitting via an AI agent would resolve the rejects.

H-BUSINESS-RULE-REJECTS.statement: Rejects recorded in DA-REJ are legitimate carrier business-rule declines (e.g., capacity, contract, routing policy) rather than data/content errors, so auto-fixing notice fields would not address the real cause and could produce improper resubmissions.

H-SYSTEMIC-UPSTREAM-DATA-ISSUE.statement: Rejects stem from a systemic upstream data-quality or process defect at ORG-A (e.g., recurring master-data or process-step error in P-1) rather than isolated per-notice mistakes, requiring a governance/process fix instead of a per-instance auto-fix agent.

H-CARRIER-SIDE-PROCESSING-ERRO.statement: ORG-B's own interface or validation logic is misclassifying valid notices as rejects (false rejects), even though the handoff H-1 itself is HEALTHY and semantically VALID, meaning the fix belongs on the carrier side, not an ORG-A auto-fix agent.

H-CARRIER-FLAKY-TRANSIENT.statement: Rejects are caused by intermittent/transient malfunctions in ORG-B's carrier system (not content errors or deliberate business rules), so blind resubmission without content fixes would resolve them.

H-CONTENT-ERRORS-FIXABLE-INDEP.statement: Shipment notices sent by ORG-A contain field-level content errors (unknown location codes affecting N-1/N-2; event-order sequencing issues affecting N-3) that cause carrier (ORG-B) rejects, as evidenced by the recorded reject reason codes — independent of and narrower than the requester's claim that an AI auto-fix agent would resolve them.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The carrier reject log records 3 rejects: N-1 and N-2 reason LOC_UNKNOWN, N-3 reason EVENT_ORDER. These are data/field-level reason codes (unknown location, event ordering), not capacity/contract/routing business-rule declines, and two of three share the same reason.

E-02.content: The carrier system is flaky; just resubmit everything.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-REQ (ORG-A, non-authoritative) frames the rejects as caused by a flaky carrier system and recommends blanket resubmission without content fixes, a framing that conflicts with the authoritative E-01 evidence showing specific field-level reason codes (LOC_UNKNOWN, EVENT_ORDER) rather than generic transient failures.

U-SYSTEMIC-VS-ISOLATED.question: Do the LOC_UNKNOWN/EVENT_ORDER errors stem from a systemic upstream data/process defect in P-1 (recurring master-data or step error) rather than isolated per-notice mistakes?
U-SYSTEMIC-VS-ISOLATED.decision_impact: If systemic, a per-notice auto-fix agent would not address the root cause and a governance/process fix in P-1 is needed instead.
U-SYSTEMIC-VS-ISOLATED.resolution_path: Review P-1 process steps and data lineage for N-1, N-2, N-3 and additional historical rejects to detect a recurring upstream pattern.
U-SYSTEMIC-VS-ISOLATED.safe_placeholder: Scope the initial fix to per-notice correction only; defer any upstream process redesign until investigated.

U-CARRIER-SIDE-FALSE-REJECT.question: Could ORG-B's own interface/validation logic be misclassifying valid notices as rejects, rather than the notices actually being erroneous?
U-CARRIER-SIDE-FALSE-REJECT.decision_impact: If true, the fix belongs on the carrier side and an ORG-A auto-fix-and-resubmit agent would not resolve, and could mask, the real defect.
U-CARRIER-SIDE-FALSE-REJECT.resolution_path: Obtain or confirm ORG-B's validation logic, or independently cross-check sample notice content against the reject reasons before assuming the fault is on ORG-A's side.
U-CARRIER-SIDE-FALSE-REJECT.safe_placeholder: Require human review/approval of each proposed fix before resubmission rather than fully autonomous correction.

U-REJECT-LOG-COMPLETENESS.question: Are the 3 records in DA-REJ the full reject population or a filtered sample/time window?
U-REJECT-LOG-COMPLETENESS.decision_impact: Affects whether current reject counts and reason-code mix can be trusted as a baseline for measuring improvement.
U-REJECT-LOG-COMPLETENESS.resolution_path: Confirm with the reject-log source/ORG-B whether the query covers the full reject history or a limited window.
U-REJECT-LOG-COMPLETENESS.safe_placeholder: Treat the current reject_count as directional only, not a final baseline, pending confirmation.

U-NO-RESUBMISSION-TOOL.question: No write-capable tool to resubmit notices to ORG-B exists in the current tool surface (only read-only reject-log) — how will corrected notices actually be resubmitted?
U-NO-RESUBMISSION-TOOL.decision_impact: Without an authorized resubmission interface, the auto-fix-and-resubmit automation cannot be executed as requested.
U-NO-RESUBMISSION-TOOL.resolution_path: Identify and authorize a write-capable interface/tool to ORG-B before building resubmission automation.
U-NO-RESUBMISSION-TOOL.safe_placeholder: Perform corrections and resubmission manually (human-executed) until an authorized tool exists.

A-FIXABLE-ERRORS.statement: The LOC_UNKNOWN and EVENT_ORDER reject reasons represent correctable content defects in the notices rather than an unresolvable carrier-side validation issue.

A-SAMPLE-REPRESENTATIVE.statement: The 3 rejects recorded in DA-REJ are representative of the overall reject problem; DA-REJ completeness is actually UNKNOWN.

A-TRANSPORT-NOT-CAUSE.statement: Handoff H-1 being HEALTHY and semantically VALID means the transmission channel itself is not contributing to the content-level errors causing rejects.

SC-TARGET-REASON.statement: Any remediation must target the actual recorded reject reasons (LOC_UNKNOWN, EVENT_ORDER) rather than assuming generic carrier flakiness.
SC-TARGET-REASON.threshold: fix mapped 1:1 to recorded reason code per notice
SC-TARGET-REASON.validation_method: Audit each corrected notice against its DA-REJ reason code before resubmission.

SC-HUMAN-GATE-RESUBMIT.statement: Resubmission of corrected notices to the external carrier system occurs only after Human Gate approval.
SC-HUMAN-GATE-RESUBMIT.validation_method: Verify a Human Gate approval record precedes every resubmit_shipment_notice execution.

SC-REDUCE-REJECT-RATE.statement: Reduce the carrier reject rate after remediation relative to the established baseline.
SC-REDUCE-REJECT-RATE.threshold: lower than baseline once baseline is confirmed
SC-REDUCE-REJECT-RATE.validation_method: Compare reject_rate metric before and after fix rollout over a defined measurement window.

VOB-U-SYSTEMIC-VS-ISOLATED.unresolved_question: Do the LOC_UNKNOWN/EVENT_ORDER errors stem from a systemic upstream data/process defect in P-1 (recurring master-data or step error) rather than isolated per-notice mistakes?

VOB-U-SYSTEMIC-VS-ISOLATED.validation_method: Review P-1 process steps and data lineage for N-1, N-2, N-3 and additional historical rejects to detect a recurring upstream pattern.

VOB-U-CARRIER-SIDE-FALSE-REJECT.unresolved_question: Could ORG-B's own interface/validation logic be misclassifying valid notices as rejects, rather than the notices actually being erroneous?
VOB-U-CARRIER-SIDE-FALSE-REJECT.reason_deferred: deferred at DEFINE Gate; safe placeholder: Require human review/approval of each proposed fix before resubmission rather than fully autonomous correction.
VOB-U-CARRIER-SIDE-FALSE-REJECT.validation_method: Obtain or confirm ORG-B's validation logic, or independently cross-check sample notice content against the reject reasons before assuming the fault is on ORG-A's side.

VOB-U-NO-RESUBMISSION-TOOL.unresolved_question: No write-capable tool to resubmit notices to ORG-B exists in the current tool surface (only read-only reject-log) — how will corrected notices actually be resubmitted?
VOB-U-NO-RESUBMISSION-TOOL.reason_deferred: deferred at DEFINE Gate; safe placeholder: Perform corrections and resubmission manually (human-executed) until an authorized tool exists.
VOB-U-NO-RESUBMISSION-TOOL.validation_method: Identify and authorize a write-capable interface/tool to ORG-B before building resubmission automation.

problem_definition.requested_solution: Let an AI agent auto-fix rejected shipment notices and resubmit them (requester's proposed remediation, SH-REQ, CL-01).
symptoms: Carrier (ORG-B) rejects shipment notices sent by ORG-A: reject log DA-REJ records 3 rejects — N-1 (LOC_UNKNOWN), N-2 (LOC_UNKNOWN), N-3 (EVENT_ORDER) — each requiring correction and resubmission before the shipment can proceed.
problem_definition.root_problem: Shipment notices ORG-A sends to carrier ORG-B are being rejected because the notices contain field-level content errors — unknown/invalid location data (notices N-1, N-2) and incorrect event ordering (notice N-3) — as recorded by the carrier reject log's specific reason codes (LOC_UNKNOWN, EVENT_ORDER), rather than carrier-side business-rule declines or generic system flakiness.

trace.summary: Shipment notices ORG-A sends to carrier ORG-B are being rejected because the notices contain field-level content errors — unknown/invalid location data (notices N-1, N-2) and incorrect event ordering (notice N-3) — as recorded by the carrier reject log's specific reason codes (LOC_UNKNOWN, EVENT_ORDER), rather than carrier-side business-rule declines or generic system flakiness.

details.requested_solution: Let an AI agent auto-fix rejected shipment notices and resubmit them (requester's proposed remediation, SH-REQ, CL-01).

trace.summary: Per why_agent_needed, judgment is needed to interpret whether the 3 recorded reasons indicate a systemic vs isolated defect and to prepare the ORG-B joint review (SR-R3), work no deterministic rule fully replaces while U-SYSTEMIC-VS-ISOLATED and U-CARRIER-SIDE-FALSE-REJECT remain open.

structural_remedies.description: Add a pre-submission validation/correction step in P-1 (location-code lookup against master data, event-sequence check) so LOC_UNKNOWN/EVENT_ORDER errors are caught before transmission.
structural_remedies.rationale: P-1.steps are empty in state, so the process logic needed to design this rule is unavailable; building/validating it exceeds remaining 225 min without that detail.; residual gap: Only fully addresses root cause if defects are systemic (H-SYSTEMIC-UPSTREAM-DATA-ISSUE still CANDIDATE); leaves U-CARRIER-SIDE-FALSE-REJECT open and provides no resubmission channel.

structural_remedies.description: Establish a write-capable resubmission integration/contract with ORG-B over H-1 (tool_surface currently only exposes read-only reject-log), closing U-NO-RESUBMISSION-TOOL.
structural_remedies.rationale: Requires cross-org technical/contractual setup with ORG-B (SH-INT) unlikely to complete inside the remaining contest budget.; residual gap: Does not fix underlying content errors; U-CARRIER-SIDE-FALSE-REJECT and U-SYSTEMIC-VS-ISOLATED remain unresolved before any resubmission is safe.

structural_remedies.description: Initiate a joint ORG-A/ORG-B (SH-INT) review of ORG-B's validation logic and request the full reject population, to resolve U-CARRIER-SIDE-FALSE-REJECT and U-REJECT-LOG-COMPLETENESS.
structural_remedies.rationale: This is a governance/data-request action initiable within the DESIGN phase budget, though ORG-B's response time is outside this agent's control.; residual gap: Clarifies the picture but does not itself correct the 3 flagged notices or build any fix/resubmit mechanism.

decision_log.rationale: causal chain: ORG-A's shipment-notice process (P-1) produces notices carrying field-level content defects (missing/invalid location reference; mis-sequenced event data). → The notices are transmitted to ORG-B over handoff H-1, which is transport-healthy and schema-valid, so the content defect is not caught before delivery. → ORG-B's reject validation evaluates notice content and flags LOC_UNKNOWN (N-1, N-2) and EVENT_ORDER (N-3) as the reject reasons (E-01). → The notices are rejected and must be corrected and resubmitted before the shipment can proceed, producing the observed backlog of carrier rejects.; rejected framings: [('H-BUSINESS-RULE-REJECTS', 'Status REJECTED; contradicted by E-01/E-02 — reject-log shows field-level reason codes (LOC_UNKNOWN, EVENT_ORDER), not capacity/contract/routing business-rule declines.'), ('H-CARRIER-FLAKY-TRANSIENT', 'Rests only on non-authoritative stakeholder claim (E-02/CL-02); authoritative E-01 shows specific, repeated, reason-coded rejects rather than generic transient/random failures, so this framing is not adopted as the premise.')]

proposal.root_problem: Shipment notices sent by ORG-A to carrier ORG-B via handoff H-1 are rejected because of field-level content errors — unresolved/missing location data (LOC_UNKNOWN, notices N-1 and N-2) and incorrect event sequencing (EVENT_ORDER, notice N-3) — as recorded in the authoritative carrier reject log, rather than carrier business-rule declines or generic carrier-system flakiness.
proposal.requested_solution: Deploy an AI agent to auto-fix the content of rejected shipment notices and resubmit them to the carrier.
symptoms: Carrier reject log (DA-REJ) records 3 rejected shipment notices: N-1 and N-2 with reason LOC_UNKNOWN, N-3 with reason EVENT_ORDER (E-01).
Two of the three rejects share the same reason code (LOC_UNKNOWN), indicating a recurring field-level issue rather than three unrelated failures (E-01).
Rejected notices currently require manual intervention to be corrected and resubmitted.
causal_chain: ORG-A's shipment notice process (P-1) produces notices in which the location field is sometimes unresolved and event ordering is sometimes incorrect (E-01).
These notices are transmitted to ORG-B via handoff H-1, which is itself HEALTHY and semantically VALID.
ORG-B's carrier intake validation flags the field-level issues and rejects the notices, logging reason codes LOC_UNKNOWN (N-1, N-2) and EVENT_ORDER (N-3) in DA-REJ (E-01).
Without an automated correction step, rejected notices sit unresolved until a person manually fixes and resubmits them, creating processing delay.

assumptions.statement: The 3 records currently in DA-REJ represent the ongoing reject pattern and not a one-off/complete historical anomaly.
The LOC_UNKNOWN and EVENT_ORDER reason codes indicate correctable sender-side field errors rather than carrier-side validation misclassifying valid data.
Resolving rejects only requires correcting notice fields on the ORG-A side; no change to ORG-B's carrier validation logic is needed, consistent with H-1 being HEALTHY/VALID.

unknowns.resolution_path: Confirm with ORG-B or the reject-log tool whether DA-REJ reflects all rejects or a subset, e.g. by checking completeness metadata or cross-referencing a longer time window.
unknowns.safe_placeholder: Treat the current reject_count (3) as a lower bound and scope the auto-fix agent to the 3 known notices before scaling to a broader population.

unknowns.question: Are the LOC_UNKNOWN/EVENT_ORDER rejects genuine sender-side content errors, or is ORG-B's own validation logic misclassifying otherwise-valid notices (H-CARRIER-SIDE-PROCESSING-ERRO)?

unknowns.resolution_path: Compare the rejected notices' location and event-order field values against ORG-A master data/schema to determine whether the values were actually invalid versus validly formatted but misread by the carrier.
unknowns.safe_placeholder: Require human review of each proposed field fix before resubmission rather than fully autonomous correction.

The requester (SH-REQ, ORG-A) initially framed the cause as a flaky carrier system and asked for blanket resubmission (CL-02, E-02), and separately proposed an AI agent to auto-fix and resubmit rejected notices (CL-01). A prior proposal was rejected (recent_events seq 36) for resting on the requester's own framing (H-CONTENT-ERRORS-FIXABLE) rather than independently established evidence, prompting the narrower, evidence-grounded framing eventually used in PD-1.

The DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS (recent_events seq 49), deferring three HIGH-criticality unknowns to verification obligations: whether errors are systemic vs. isolated (VOB-U-SYSTEMIC-VS-ISOLATED), whether ORG-B's own validation is falsely rejecting valid notices (VOB-U-CARRIER-SIDE-FALSE-REJECT), and the absence of any write-capable resubmission tool (VOB-U-NO-RESUBMISSION-TOOL).

This is because the three open VOBs' blocking_scope (correct_notice_field_errors:P-1 and resubmit_shipment_notice:H-1) falls outside the actually-released scope (diagnose/monitor only), so the released capabilities could proceed despite those unresolved unknowns.

proposal.summary: The problem, as established from the carrier reject log, is that ORG-A's shipment notices to carrier ORG-B are rejected due to field-level content errors: unknown/invalid location codes on notices N-1 and N-2 (LOC_UNKNOWN) and incorrect event ordering on N-3 (EVENT_ORDER) (E-01, F-01). This was determined by weighing the authoritative reject-log evidence against the requester's (SH-REQ) non-authoritative claim that the carrier is simply "flaky" and needs blanket resubmission (CL-02, E-02); the specific, repeated reason codes supported the content-error hypothesis (H-CONTENT-ERRORS-FIXABLE, SUPPORTED) and refuted a generic business-rule-decline hypothesis (H-BUSINESS-RULE-REJECTS, REJECTED). An earlier proposal was itself rejected for leaning too heavily on the requester's framing, leading to the independently-evidenced problem definition (PD-1) that was ultimately used, which received a CONDITIONAL_PASS at the DEFINE gate due to several deferred high-criticality unknowns. Given that, the release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with nothing on hold: only the diagnosis (diagnose_reject_reasons:DA-REJ) and monitoring (monitor_reject_rate:DA-REJ) capabilities were released, because the open verification obligations about systemic-vs-isolated errors, possible carrier-side false rejects, and the complete lack of a write-capable resubmission tool all block the auto-fix and resubmit actions (correct_notice_field_errors:P-1, resubmit_shipment_notice:H-1) specifically, not the diagnose/monitor scope that was actually shipped. In plain terms: you now have a verified read of why notices are being rejected and ongoing tracking of that reason mix, but the system does not yet auto-fix or resubmit anything, and several important open questions (data completeness, systemic vs. isolated cause, possible carrier-side false rejects, missing resubmission channel) remain unresolved and documented as known limitations rather than silently ignored.
